chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūsuf ibn ʿAqīl, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام gave judgment concerning a group who slaughtered a camel and ate it. They were examined as to which of them had slaughtered it, and they testified against themselves that they had all slaughtered it together, not singling out any one person apart from another. So he judged that their right hands be cut off.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام as the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.شَهِدُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ: they testified against themselves in confession
key_terms.قَضَى: he gave a legal judgment or judicial ruling
key_terms.نَحَرُوا: they slaughtered by piercing the throat of the animal

ai.seo_question: What was the ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام when several people jointly slaughtered and ate a stolen camel?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a legal judgment of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding a group who jointly slaughtered and consumed a camel. When they collectively confessed to equal participation, he ruled collectively against them, showing the application of judicial procedure and penal law in a case of shared criminal liability.
